indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the committed uv checksums to the pinned required-version (or single-source them) so a version bump without matching checksums fails lint, not just runtime.
evidence: action.yml:65 `$url = "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/$version/$asset"` downloads the version-specific artifact
scripts/check_uv_pin.py:287 `for name, expected in REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS.items():` compares action env against a hardcoded dict, not against the pinned version
pyproject.toml:346 `required-version = "==0.12.7"` is the only place the version lives; the guard never cross-references the checksums to it
ABSENCE: no check asserts the checksums belong to `$version`, so version/checksum skew is invisible to lint
indeterminate.finding: The pinned uv version (required-version) and the committed sha256 checksums are decoupled: neither check_uv_pin.py nor action.yml ties the six UV_SHA256_* values to the version string. Bumping [tool.uv] required-version without updating the checksums passes `make lint` (REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS still matches the stale action.yml env) and only fails later at runtime with a checksum mismatch on the runner.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the action's version regex and the guard's _is_exact_specifier on the same accepted exact-pin shape.
evidence: action.yml:32 `'^required-version\s*=\s*"==([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+)"...` requires >=1 dot group
scripts/check_uv_pin.py:93 `return all(part.isdigit() for part in remainder.split(".") if part != "")` accepts a dotless `==5`
indeterminate.finding: The action's PowerShell version regex requires at least two dotted components (`[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)+`), while the Python guard's _is_exact_specifier accepts a single-component pin like `==5`. The two readers disagree on what a valid exact pin is, so a pyproject value the guard accepts could be rejected by the action at runtime.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin `actions/cache` in .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml to a full commit SHA (with a version comment) to match the repo's SHA-pinning policy.
evidence: .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml: "uses: actions/cache@v6"

tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py: "if u.startswith(\"./\"):  continue" then "ref = ... assert re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9a-f]{40}\", ref)" — the local action path is skipped, so cache@v6 inside it is never SHA-checked
Existing workflows SHA-pin everything, e.g. "astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891fec2bb8e7d6c99fc78c9fec3a63790f8d" and "actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97"
indeterminate.finding: The new local composite action pins the third-party `actions/cache` dependency to the mutable major tag `actions/cache@v6` rather than a full 40-char commit SHA, bypassing the repo's SHA-pinning invariant which the release-pin test only enforces on top-level workflow `uses:` lines.
scenarios: actions/cache@v6 tag is force-moved to a compromised commit; every uv-installing CI job silently picks up the new code
indeterminate.suggested_fix: Replace `uses: actions/cache@v6` with `uses: actions/cache@<40-char-sha>  # v6.x` and extend check_uv_pin.py to assert nested actions in the composite action are SHA-pinned.

evidence: scripts/check_uv_pin.py REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS mirrors the six env hashes and check_local_action asserts `actual != expected` only against this in-repo copy
action.yml verifies download against `$expectedHash` sourced from the same committed env — no external attestation (no `gh attestation verify`, cosign, or SLSA provenance) is performed
ABSENCE: no reference to upstream signed digests / provenance in action.yml or check_uv_pin.py
indeterminate.finding: The committed uv artifact SHA-256 checksums are asserted only for internal consistency (action.yml env vs check_uv_pin.py REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS), with no verification that they match astral-sh's upstream-published/attested digests for the pinned uv version, so a wrong-but-consistent hash would pass the guard.
scenarios: A future uv-version bump commits a checksum that does not match astral-sh's real release; all internal checks still pass and CI installs an unverified binary

No test in test_uv_pin_guard.py removes the enable-cache input or the actions/cache step from ACTION_CLEAN; named violating inputs: an action.yml with no `inputs.enable-cache`, and one with no `actions/cache` step
indeterminate.finding: The malformed-checksum branch (wrong length or non-hex characters) added at scripts/check_uv_pin.py:291 has no test. Tests cover a MISSING checksum env entry and a checksum MISMATCH, but never a value that is present-and-not-64-hex, so the 'is malformed' Finding path is regression-blind.
merged_from: The second forbidden-manifest token 'Fetching manifest data' in FORBIDDEN_ACTION_TEXT is never exercised. Only 'raw.githubusercontent.com' has a failing test, so a regression that drops or mis-handles the second token would not be caught.

The new enable-cache contract assertions have no failing test: neither the 'must define the enable-cache input' branch (check_uv_pin.py:281-282) nor the 'must wire enable-cache through actions/cache' branch (:283-284) is exercised by a skew test.
scenarios: A checksum env value is truncated or contains an uppercase/non-hex character; the malformed branch would need to fire but is unverified
indeterminate.suggested_fix: Add a test that replaces one checksum value with a 10-char non-hex string in ACTION_CLEAN and asserts returncode 1 and 'malformed' in stderr.
